entries.remember: Do not use when an intact gag reflex is present.

entries.summary: Breathing difficulty when lying flat.
entries.details: Use the term in a complete patient-care sentence to reinforce meaning.
entries.remember: Spelling and exact definitions may vary slightly by source.

entries.summary: Medical gas used to correct suspected or confirmed hypoxemia and support critically ill patients.
entries.details: Indications depend on patient condition and local protocol. Titrate when appropriate; avoid delaying ventilation or airway management.
entries.remember: Delivery device, flow, target saturation, response, fire risk.

entries.summary: Unusual paleness.
entries.details: Use the term in a complete patient-care sentence to reinforce meaning.
entries.remember: Spelling and exact definitions may vary slightly by source.

entries.summary: Number of pregnancies reaching a defined viable gestational age, with local notation conventions varying.
entries.details: Clarify the system used when documenting a detailed obstetric history.
entries.remember: Para is not simply the number of living children.

entries.summary: Abnormal sensation such as tingling or numbness.
entries.details: Use the term in a complete patient-care sentence to reinforce meaning.
entries.remember: Spelling and exact definitions may vary slightly by source.

entries.summary: Pull, Aim, Squeeze, Sweep.
entries.details: Basic extinguisher use when safe and appropriate.
entries.remember: Use mnemonics as prompts, not substitutes for clinical judgment.

entries.summary: How disease or injury changes normal body function.
entries.details: Use the term in a complete patient-care sentence to reinforce meaning.
entries.remember: Spelling and exact definitions may vary slightly by source.

entries.summary: Patient care report documenting assessment, care, response, and disposition.
entries.details: Write an accurate, chronological, objective record using approved terminology and required data elements.
entries.remember: Document what you observed and did, not what you assume.

entries.summary: Rapid visual assessment of appearance, work of breathing, and circulation to skin.
entries.details: Use before touching the child to form an initial impression and identify urgency.
entries.remember: The PAT is an impression, not a complete assessment.

entries.summary: Inability to maintain adequate oxygenation or ventilation.
entries.details: Signs include fatigue, poor air movement, altered mental status, bradycardia, cyanosis, or irregular breathing.
entries.remember: A slowing rate in a tiring child may be worsening.

entries.summary: Inadequate tissue perfusion in a child.
entries.details: Tachycardia, delayed capillary refill, weak pulses, altered behavior, and cool skin may precede hypotension.
entries.remember: Hypotension is a late pediatric shock sign.

entries.summary: Circumferential device for suspected unstable pelvic injury.
entries.details: Placement is typically over the greater trochanters, per training.
entries.remember: Use equipment only within training, authorization, and manufacturer guidance.

entries.summary: Device used to stabilize a suspected unstable pelvic injury.
entries.details: Apply over the greater trochanters, not the waist, following device instructions and local protocol.
entries.remember: Correct position is lower than many learners expect.

entries.summary: Delivery of oxygenated blood to tissues.
entries.details: Use the term in a complete patient-care sentence to reinforce meaning.
entries.remember: Spelling and exact definitions may vary slightly by source.

entries.summary: Pupils Equal, Round, Reactive to Light.
entries.details: Add size, gaze, and other findings when relevant.
entries.remember: Use mnemonics as prompts, not substitutes for clinical judgment.

entries.summary: Relevant finding that was specifically assessed and found absent.
entries.details: Include negatives that help distinguish serious conditions or support decisions.
entries.remember: Do not chart a checklist of things you never assessed.

entries.summary: Pulse, Motor, Sensation / Circulation, Sensation, Movement.
entries.details: Document before and after splinting or movement.
entries.remember: Use mnemonics as prompts, not substitutes for clinical judgment.

entries.summary: Toward the back of the body.
entries.details: Use the term in a complete patient-care sentence to reinforce meaning.
entries.remember: Spelling and exact definitions may vary slightly by source.

entries.summary: Excessive bleeding after delivery.
entries.details: Recognize rapidly, support circulation, perform protocol-directed uterine massage when indicated, and transport promptly.
entries.remember: Estimate bleeding poorly? Describe soaked materials and ongoing flow.

entries.summary: Pregnancy-related hypertensive disorder with potential organ dysfunction.
entries.details: Symptoms may include headache, visual changes, edema, right upper abdominal pain, and hypertension.
entries.remember: Severe headache late in pregnancy is a warning sign.

entries.summary: Common EMS teaching range: roughly 80-140/min.
entries.details: Trend and appearance matter more than one isolated number.
entries.remember: Ranges are teaching references, not universal treatment thresholds.

entries.summary: Common EMS teaching range: roughly 22-34/min.
entries.details: Retractions, grunting, and nasal flaring are important.
entries.remember: Ranges are teaching references, not universal treatment thresholds.

entries.summary: Dressing designed to maintain pressure over a bleeding wound.
entries.details: Do not obscure ongoing reassessment of bleeding and distal circulation.
entries.remember: Use equipment only within training, authorization, and manufacturer guidance.

entries.summary: Feeling of near-fainting without full loss of consciousness.
entries.details: Use the term in a complete patient-care sentence to reinforce meaning.
entries.remember: Spelling and exact definitions may vary slightly by source.

entries.summary: Rapid search for immediate threats to airway, breathing, circulation, disability, and exposure.
entries.details: Control catastrophic hemorrhage, manage airway and breathing, support perfusion, and determine transport priority.
entries.remember: Treat life threats as you find them.

entries.summary: Closer to the trunk or point of origin.
entries.details: Use the term in a complete patient-care sentence to reinforce meaning.
entries.remember: Spelling and exact definitions may vary slightly by source.

entries.summary: Noninvasive estimate of oxygen saturation and pulse rate.
entries.details: Confirm waveform/perfusion and compare displayed pulse with palpated pulse.
entries.remember: Use equipment only within training, authorization, and manufacturer guidance.

entries.summary: Rescue, Alarm, Confine, Extinguish/Evacuate.
entries.details: Common fire-response mnemonic in facilities; follow site policy.
entries.remember: Use mnemonics as prompts, not substitutes for clinical judgment.

entries.summary: Brief prearrival communication to the receiving facility.
entries.details: Include unit, age, chief problem, important history, critical findings, treatment, response, and ETA according to local expectations.
entries.remember: Keep it short enough to be heard and complete enough to prepare.

entries.summary: Repeat evaluation to identify change or treatment response.
entries.details: Use the term in a complete patient-care sentence to reinforce meaning.
entries.remember: Spelling and exact definitions may vary slightly by source.

entries.summary: Patient decision not to accept recommended assessment, treatment, or transport.
entries.details: Assess decision-making capacity, explain risks and alternatives, follow protocol, document thoroughly, and provide return precautions.
entries.remember: A signature alone does not make a refusal valid.

entries.summary: Low-pitched coarse sounds often associated with secretions.
entries.details: Use the term in a complete patient-care sentence to reinforce meaning.
entries.remember: Spelling and exact definitions may vary slightly by source.

entries.summary: Signs/symptoms, Allergies, Medications, Past history, Last oral intake, Events leading up.
entries.details: Use to organize history; ask follow-up questions rather than treating it as a script.
entries.remember: Use mnemonics as prompts, not substitutes for clinical judgment.

entries.summary: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation.
entries.details: Structured handoff or consultation format.
entries.remember: Use mnemonics as prompts, not substitutes for clinical judgment.

entries.summary: Communication structure: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation.
entries.details: Useful for organized clinical communication and escalation.
entries.remember: State the immediate concern first.

entries.summary: Initial process used to identify hazards, resources, mechanism or nature of illness, and patient count.
entries.details: Continue size-up throughout the call because conditions can change.
entries.remember: Scene safety is ongoing, not a one-time checkbox.

entries.summary: Common EMS teaching range: roughly 70-120/min.
entries.details: Use local pediatric reference tools.
entries.remember: Ranges are teaching references, not universal treatment thresholds.

entries.summary: Common EMS teaching range: roughly 18-30/min.
entries.details: Consider fever, anxiety, pain, and exertion.
entries.remember: Ranges are teaching references, not universal treatment thresholds.

entries.summary: Split stretcher that can be assembled around a patient.
entries.details: Useful for selected lifts and transfers; follow manufacturer limits.
entries.remember: Use equipment only within training, authorization, and manufacturer guidance.

entries.summary: Episode of abnormal electrical activity in the brain.
entries.details: Protect from injury, manage airway and oxygenation, check glucose, identify duration and recurrence, and assess for causes.
entries.remember: Postictal confusion is expected, but persistent abnormalities need reassessment.

entries.summary: Life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by an abnormal response to infection.
entries.details: Look for suspected infection plus abnormal temperature, mental status, respiratory rate, perfusion, blood pressure, or glucose. Follow local screening and alert criteria.
entries.remember: Sepsis may present without fever.

entries.summary: Salivation, Lacrimation, Urination, Defecation, GI upset, Emesis.
entries.details: Cholinergic toxidrome reminder; some versions add miosis/bronchorrhea.
entries.remember: Use mnemonics as prompts, not substitutes for clinical judgment.

entries.summary: Subjective, Objective, Assessment, Plan.
entries.details: Documentation framework; EMS PCR structure may differ.
entries.remember: Use mnemonics as prompts, not substitutes for clinical judgment.

entries.summary: Documentation format: Subjective, Objective, Assessment, Plan.
entries.details: Useful for organizing symptoms, findings, impression, and care.
entries.remember: Choose a format that preserves chronology and clinical reasoning.

entries.summary: Alkalinizing medication used in selected toxicologic and resuscitation situations.
entries.details: Not a routine medication for all arrests. Follow protocol.
entries.remember: Ventilation, indication, IV compatibility.

entries.summary: Strategies used to minimize movement when spinal injury risk is present.
entries.details: Use assessment-based indications and the least harmful effective method allowed by local protocol.
entries.remember: A rigid collar is only one part of motion restriction.

entries.summary: Chair designed to move selected patients on stairs or through tight spaces.
entries.details: Use straps, adequate personnel, and safe lifting technique.
entries.remember: Use equipment only within training, authorization, and manufacturer guidance.

entries.summary: Actions used to reduce exposure to blood, body fluids, and infectious material.
entries.details: Select PPE based on anticipated exposure and perform hand hygiene and equipment cleaning.
entries.remember: PPE should match the hazard.

entries.summary: Prolonged or repeated seizures without adequate recovery.
entries.details: A time-critical emergency requiring airway support, rapid assessment, and protocol-directed medication at the appropriate provider level.
entries.remember: Track seizure start and stop times.

entries.summary: Acoustic device for breath sounds, blood pressure, and selected cardiac sounds.
entries.details: Good seal, correct earpiece direction, quiet technique.
entries.remember: Use equipment only within training, authorization, and manufacturer guidance.

entries.summary: Harsh upper-airway sound, often inspiratory.
entries.details: Use the term in a complete patient-care sentence to reinforce meaning.
entries.remember: Spelling and exact definitions may vary slightly by source.

entries.summary: Harsh high-pitched sound caused by upper-airway narrowing.
entries.details: Often heard on inspiration and may signal severe airway compromise. Minimize agitation and prepare for rapid deterioration.
entries.remember: Stridor is an airway warning, not merely a lung sound.

entries.summary: Acute neurologic injury caused by interrupted blood flow or bleeding in the brain.
entries.details: Determine last known well, perform a validated stroke assessment, check glucose, identify anticoagulant use, and transport to an appropriate facility.
entries.remember: Time last known well, not time found.

entries.summary: Device used to remove secretions, blood, or vomit from the airway.
entries.details: Check power, tubing, canister, catheter, and function before calls.
entries.remember: Use equipment only within training, authorization, and manufacturer guidance.

entries.summary: Removal of blood, vomit, mucus, or other material from the airway.
entries.details: Prepare suction early, visualize when possible, limit each attempt, and reoxygenate or ventilate between attempts as needed.
entries.remember: Suction before trying to ventilate through contamination.

entries.summary: Above or toward the head.
entries.details: Use the term in a complete patient-care sentence to reinforce meaning.
entries.remember: Spelling and exact definitions may vary slightly by source.

entries.summary: Advanced airway device seated above the vocal cords.
entries.details: Confirm placement with waveform capnography when available and ongoing reassessment.
entries.remember: Use equipment only within training, authorization, and manufacturer guidance.

entries.summary: Temporary loss of consciousness from reduced cerebral perfusion.
entries.details: Use the term in a complete patient-care sentence to reinforce meaning.
entries.remember: Spelling and exact definitions may vary slightly by source.

entries.summary: Brief loss of consciousness from transient reduction in cerebral perfusion.
entries.details: Assess for cardiac, neurologic, hemorrhagic, metabolic, medication, and situational causes. Obtain orthostatic findings only when safe and allowed.
entries.remember: Syncope is a symptom, not a diagnosis.

entries.summary: Abnormally rapid heart rate.
entries.details: Use the term in a complete patient-care sentence to reinforce meaning.
entries.remember: Spelling and exact definitions may vary slightly by source.

entries.summary: Abnormally rapid breathing.
entries.details: Use the term in a complete patient-care sentence to reinforce meaning.
entries.remember: Spelling and exact definitions may vary slightly by source.

entries.summary: Progressive pressure in the chest impairing ventilation and circulation.
entries.details: Suspect with severe respiratory distress, asymmetric breath sounds, chest trauma, and shock. Advanced treatment depends on scope and protocol.
entries.remember: Do not wait for every textbook sign.

entries.summary: Common EMS teaching range: roughly 90-150/min.
entries.details: Crying and fever can increase rate.
entries.remember: Ranges are teaching references, not universal treatment thresholds.

entries.summary: Common EMS teaching range: roughly 24-40/min.
entries.details: Observe before touching when possible.
entries.remember: Ranges are teaching references, not universal treatment thresholds.

entries.summary: Device that stops life-threatening extremity hemorrhage by circumferential compression.
entries.details: Apply for severe extremity bleeding per training; note time.
entries.remember: Use equipment only within training, authorization, and manufacturer guidance.

entries.summary: Device used to control life-threatening extremity hemorrhage.
entries.details: Place according to device instructions and protocol, tighten until bleeding stops, record time, and do not periodically loosen.
entries.remember: If bleeding continues, tighten or add a second tourniquet.

entries.summary: Formal handoff of patient responsibility to another qualified provider.
entries.details: Give a concise report, ensure understanding, transfer documentation, and note the receiving person and time.
entries.remember: Responsibility is transferred through communication, not merely arrival.

entries.summary: Temporary neurologic symptoms caused by transient cerebral ischemia.
entries.details: Symptoms may resolve before EMS arrival but still require urgent evaluation. Document the original deficit and timing.
entries.remember: Resolved symptoms are still important.

entries.summary: Heavy scissors designed to cut clothing and some soft materials.
entries.details: Protect skin while cutting; clean after use.
entries.remember: Use equipment only within training, authorization, and manufacturer guidance.

entries.summary: Brain injury caused by external force.
entries.details: Prevent hypoxia and hypotension, monitor neurologic status, identify anticoagulants, and transport appropriately.
entries.remember: Small changes in mental status matter.

entries.summary: Prioritizing patients based on urgency and resources.
entries.details: Use the term in a complete patient-care sentence to reinforce meaning.
entries.remember: Spelling and exact definitions may vary slightly by source.

entries.summary: Prioritization of multiple patients when needs exceed immediately available resources.
entries.details: Use the locally adopted system and reassess categories as conditions and resources change.
entries.remember: Triage is dynamic.

entries.summary: On one side.
entries.details: Use the term in a complete patient-care sentence to reinforce meaning.
entries.remember: Spelling and exact definitions may vary slightly by source.

entries.summary: Fixed-performance oxygen mask using interchangeable adapters.
entries.details: More common in facilities; delivers a selected oxygen concentration.
entries.remember: Use equipment only within training, authorization, and manufacturer guidance.

entries.summary: Medication dosing calculated from patient weight.
entries.details: Use measured weight when available, kilograms only, approved references, and an independent double-check.
entries.remember: Never convert or calculate mentally when a safer tool is available.

entries.summary: Musical sound associated with narrowed lower airways.
entries.details: Use the term in a complete patient-care sentence to reinforce meaning.
entries.remember: Spelling and exact definitions may vary slightly by source.

entries.summary: Musical sound caused by narrowed lower airways.
entries.details: Usually more prominent on exhalation. Assess severity, air movement, work of breathing, and response to treatment.
entries.remember: Less wheezing with worsening air movement can mean fatigue.

entries.summary: Observed effort required to breathe.
entries.details: Look for abnormal positioning, retractions, nasal flaring, head bobbing, and abnormal airway sounds.
entries.remember: Respiratory rate alone does not show work.

entries.summary: Firm placement of appropriate gauze into a deep junctional wound.
entries.details: Pack directly to the bleeding source and maintain pressure according to protocol and product guidance.
entries.remember: Fill the wound cavity; do not merely cover it.

entries.summary: Rigid suction tip for the mouth and oropharynx.
entries.details: Use under direct visualization; avoid prolonged suction.
entries.remember: Use equipment only within training, authorization, and manufacturer guidance.
